evidence.title: Restructuring of Azucarera Spanish sugar operations

initiatives.name: British Sugar Decarbonisation Investment Programme
initiatives.summary: British Sugar has invested approximately £134m since 2018 in decarbonisation initiatives including fuel switching, CHP plant upgrades, and energy efficiency programmes, achieving a cumulative reduction of over 160kt CO2e and eliminating coal usage in CHP plants in 2025.

evidence.title: British Sugar decarbonisation investment of £134m

initiatives.name: Vivergo Bioethanol Plant Closure
initiatives.summary: ABF decided to close its loss-making Vivergo bioethanol plant on Humberside after the UK government failed to provide a regulatory/financial solution to restore profitability, following the US-UK trade deal that gave tariff-free access to US ethanol suppliers. The closure resulted in significant impairment and cash costs and job losses.
initiatives.investmentSummary: £135m non-cash impairment charge plus £56m cash costs (Azucarera and Vivergo combined); separately £161m impairment/restructuring costs (£32m cash) and £30m closure costs (£24m cash) specific to Vivergo/Azucarera in FY25

timeline.first_mentioned: 2025 (closure announced following H1 results April 2025, negotiations June 2025)
timeline.latest_update: 2025 (closure announced following H1 results April 2025, negotiations June 2025)

evidence.title: Closure of Vivergo bioethanol plant
evidence.summary: ABF decided to close its loss-making Vivergo bioethanol plant on Humberside after the UK government failed to provide a regulatory/financial solution to restore profitability, following the US-UK trade deal that gave tariff-free access to US ethanol suppliers. The closure resulted in significant impairment and cash costs and job losses.
evidence.quote: We also decided to close Vivergo, our loss-making bioethanol plant on Humberside... the Group took a non-cash impairment charge of £135m and cash costs of £56m arising from Azucarera and the closure of Vivergo.

initiatives.name: Share Buyback Programmes
initiatives.summary: ABF executed multiple share buyback programmes during the year, including a £100m extension completed in November 2024, a £500m programme completed August 2025, and a new £250m programme approved to complete by end of current financial year, reflecting strong capital returns to shareholders.

evidence.title: Share buyback programmes totaling over £1 billion
evidence.summary: ABF executed multiple share buyback programmes during the year, including a £100m extension completed in November 2024, a £500m programme completed August 2025, and a new £250m programme approved to complete by end of current financial year, reflecting strong capital returns to shareholders.
evidence.quote: On 11 September 2024 we announced a £100m extension to the share buyback programme of the last financial year, which we duly completed in November 2024. We subsequently announced our third £500m share buyback programme on 5 November 2024, which we completed in August 2025... the Board has approved a further share buyback programme of £250m to be completed by the end of the current financial year.

evidence.title: Primark halve value chain emissions by 2030

evidence.quote: Under Primark Cares, the business has set an overarching objective to halve carbon emissions across its value chain by 2030 from a 2019 base year. Within the same timeframe, Primark set Science-Based Targets committing to reduce absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 50% and also reduce absolute Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services by 50%.

initiatives.name: Group Structure Strategic Review – Primark/Food Separation
initiatives.summary: The Board is conducting a strategic review of the Group structure, with Rothschild & Co assisting, which may result in a separation of the Primark and Food businesses to maximize long-term shareholder value. The review is being conducted in consultation with majority shareholder Wittington Investments.

evidence.title: Review of Group structure - potential Primark/Food separation
evidence.summary: The Board is conducting a strategic review of the Group structure, with Rothschild & Co assisting, which may result in a separation of the Primark and Food businesses to maximize long-term shareholder value. The review is being conducted in consultation with majority shareholder Wittington Investments.
evidence.quote: The Board of ABF has been conducting a review of the Group structure with a view to maximising long-term value. Although no decision has been taken, the outcome of this review may lead to the Board deciding to undertake a separation of the Primark and Food businesses.
